summary.summary: This is Cyngor Gwynedd's own 2025/26 Statement of Accounts, still marked 'Subject to Audit', going to the council's Governance and Audit Committee. The balance sheet is solid: long-term borrowing fell from £90.1m to £69.4m over the year, total reserves grew from £592.7m to £644.6m, and the unearmarked General Fund balance nearly doubled from £7.9m to £14.5m after a deliberate top-up. The Capital Financing Requirement rose to £188.5m (from £179.9m) even as external borrowing fell, meaning the council is increasingly relying on internal borrowing rather than new external debt. The narrative notes real budget pressure — a £6.6m in-year overspend concentrated in adult/children's care and waste — but there is no exceptional financial support, capitalisation direction, or section 114-type language anywhere in the document.

news_drafts.headline: North Wales Corporate Joint Committee's finance officer says a refused levy would mean a section 114 notice
news_drafts.lead:
The North Wales Corporate Joint Committee (CJC) cannot set a balanced budget without a levy on its local authorities, its section 151 officer has told a sub-committee. The officer said that if the levy were refused, "the Corporate Joint Committee would be spending illegally from 1 April 2027".

The question came from the Sub-Committee, which asked what would happen if local authorities refused to pay the levy. The section 151 officer is the council's chief finance officer, the post that carries the legal duty to issue a section 114 notice, the formal report that a body cannot balance its budget.

In that case, the officer said, they would have no choice but to issue such a notice. The exchange is recorded in the cover report to the committee's medium term financial plan.

news_drafts.headline: Gwynedd forecasts £9.8m overspend for 2026/27, £6.5m of it in children's services, and asks Cabinet to freeze spending
news_drafts.lead:
Gwynedd Council is forecasting a deficit of £9.8m on its 2026/27 budget, the position expected by March 2027 as measured at the end of August. Of that, £9.4m sits in departments and £0.4m in corporate budgets. The Cabinet on 10 November is recommended to freeze unavoidable expenditure for the rest of the financial year.

Children and Families accounts for £6.5m, or 69%, of the total, against a proposed budget of £28.2m. The paper says this assumes no change in what is provided during the year. It reports £5.7m above budget on specialist care, with more people needing care within and outside the county. Adults, Health and Well-being forecasts £2.3m over its £91.3m budget, despite more than £3.3m of additional permanent funding for 2026/27. The paper reports pressures in residential, nursing and domiciliary care. Appendix 1 shows a gross overspend of £10.9m, reduced to £9.8m by £1.1m of recommended adjustments, mainly in Environment.

The report says the council expects to use reserves at the end of the year to fund the deficit, with Cabinet to choose which, on its statutory finance officer's advice. It says the Chief Executive has met heads of department urgently and a programme to respond is in place, including continued work to achieve savings. A panel performance assessment describes a £6.6m overspend in 2024/25 as covered by exceptional corporate underspends and late Welsh Government grants.

news_drafts.headline: Gwynedd adult services overspent by £6.1m across the three years to 2025-26, committee papers show
news_drafts.lead:
Gwynedd Council's adult services department overspent its budget by a total of £6.1 million over the three years to 2025-26, according to a report on the use of data in budget planning put to the Governance and Audit Committee. The figure covers the whole of adult services, not residential care alone.

The report recommends that the lessons learned in adult residential care be applied across all services where spending follows demand. The council's Annual Governance Statement for 2025-26, in which the council speaks about itself, names overspending in both 2024/25 and 2025/26. It gives no amounts for those years.

The statement says setting a balanced budget for 2027/28 will be challenging. It says departmental budgets must be adequate for the level of service required, "to avoid overspending as seen in 2024/25 and 2025/26." It adds that increasing pressures on the budget make it harder for departments to stay within budget. The council also says a situation "can be envisaged" where there are "insufficient funds in the future to address the budget shortfall", and links this to the continuing need to find savings and to rising demand for services. It gives no figure for that shortfall. The statement says the position on day-to-day spending (revenue expenditure) is reported to the Governance and Audit Committee and to the council's Cabinet.

findings.paper_title: Revenue Report End of August 2026 Review
findings.headline: Parking and highway income targets are not being met, and the council recommends a freeze on unavoidable expenditure for the rest of the financial year.
findings.detail: The paper reports parking and highway income shortfalls and a reduction in externally commissioned highways work. It recommends that action to freeze unavoidable expenditure be implemented for the remainder of the financial year.
findings.matters: A spending freeze for the rest of the year signals the council is moving to direct control over its budget, which other councils may treat as a precedent.
findings.figures: £329k Highways, Engineering and YGC deficit; £467K Environment deficit
findings.quote: action to freeze unavoidable expenditure be implemented for the remainder of the financial year.

findings.paper_title: Revenue Report End of August 2026 Review
findings.headline: Approval sought to fund a £1.006 million Waste overspend from the Producer Extended Responsibility Fund for packaging materials.
findings.detail: The paper says the Environment Department's waste overspend will be met from the new income from a levy on packaging materials for producers and retailers, which is intended to promote recycling. It notes waste overspending is an annual trend and needs a Waste Service restructure.
findings.matters: Using extended producer responsibility income to cover a service overspend is a funding route other councils with waste pressures may be considering.
findings.figures: £1.006 million overspend; £1.006 million from the Producer Extended Responsibility Fund
findings.quote: Approve funding of the £1.006 million above budget expenditure in the field of Waste using £1.006 million from the Producer Extended Responsibility Fund for packaging materials.

findings.paper_title: Revenue Report End of August 2026 Review
findings.headline: Emergency accommodation spending is projected at £5.4 million this year, down from £6.1 million in each of the last two years, and a £800k one-off allocation is to be returned.
findings.detail: The paper attributes the reduction to deliberate interventions by the service and says it is not anticipated there will be further demand, so the £800k one-off allocation can be returned at corporate level. The council tax premium funded £4.2m of the emergency accommodation budget in 2026/27.
findings.matters: A reduction in temporary accommodation costs after years of pressure is a demand turn that other councils facing the same housing pressure will want to know about.
findings.figures: £5.4 million (2026/27); £6.1 million (last two years); £800k one-off allocation; £4.2m funded by council tax premium
findings.quote: down to £5.4 million this year compared to £6.1 million in the last two years.

findings.paper_title: Revenue Report End of August 2026 Review
findings.headline: Byw'n Iach needs £115k of council support above its contract in 2026/27, projected to fall from £550k in 2022/23.
findings.detail: The paper lists support of £550k in 2022/23, £308k in 2023/24, £281k in 2024/25 and £269k in 2025/26. It says the amount required will reduce to £115k by the end of 2026/27, which the paper says is a movement in the right direction.
findings.matters: Falling reliance on top-up payments to an arm's-length provider is a trend finance directors with similar companies will want to compare.
findings.quote: the amount required will have reduced to £115k by the end of the year.

findings.paper_title: Revenue Report End of August 2026 Review
findings.headline: Chief Executive states that managing the demand-driven deficit is beyond the Council's ability.
findings.detail: The paper says a deficit in demand is the obvious reason for most of the budget deficit. Despite an urgent meeting with heads of department and a programme to push savings, it says managing the demand-driven element is outside the Council's control.
findings.matters: A council stating in a public committee paper that demand pressures are beyond its control is a statement a lender or peer finance director would want to note.
findings.quote: managing that is beyond the Council's ability.

daily_post.headline: The Corporate Joint Committee budget total in section 6.5 (£1,200,090 for 2027/28) is £37,260 below the sum of the lines listed in its table.
daily_post.lead: A budget total that does not foot to its own lines is one a finance officer checking the paper would need to resolve before relying on the figures.
